title: 7 States, 1 River and an Agonizing Choice

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店打碟的黑胶唱片时代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着 300 件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，把 DJ 台变成一个充满 50 年历史精美文物的流动博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的萨布丽娜·塔弗尼西，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: 40 million people in seven states in the western U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国西部七个州的 4000 万人口，

sentences.en: depend on water provided by the Colorado River.
sentences.zh: 都依赖科罗拉多河提供的水源。

sentences.en: After 20 years of drought, that river has reached a breaking point.
sentences.zh: 经过 20 年的干旱，这条河流已经到了崩溃的边缘。

sentences.en: And those seven states were supposed to come up with a deal to cut their use of that water by today.
sentences.zh: 而这七个州本应在今天之前达成一项削减用水量的协议。

sentences.en: My colleague Christopher Flavel explains why the federal government may now have to step in and make an agonizing choice.
sentences.zh: 我的同事克里斯托弗·弗拉维尔将解释为什么联邦政府现在可能不得不介入，并做出一个痛苦的选择。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, January 31St.
sentences.zh: 今天是 1 月 31 日，星期二。

sentences.en: Chris, we know the water situation in the west is pretty bad.
sentences.zh: 克里斯，我们知道西部的水资源状况相当糟糕。

sentences.en: But you've reported now that the problem and that the effort to solve the problem has come to a crisis point.
sentences.zh: 但你现在的报道显示，这个问题以及解决问题的努力已经到了危急关头。

sentences.en: So, tell me about that.
sentences.zh: 那么，跟我说说具体情况吧。

sentences.en: What's going on?
sentences.zh: 到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: So, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 是这样的，美国西部

sentences.en: has had a drought in the west since 2000.
sentences.zh: 自 2000 年以来一直处于干旱状态。

sentences.en: And that's meant a lot of things.
sentences.zh: 这意味着很多问题。

sentences.en: But one of them is that the Colorado River, which provides water to about 40 million people in seven states, is drying up.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是为七个州约 4000 万人提供水源的科罗拉多河正在干涸。

sentences.en: Those states are Arizona, Nevada, California, Wyoming, Utah, New Mexico, and Colorado.
sentences.zh: 这些州分别是亚利桑那州、内华达州、加利福尼亚州、怀俄明州、犹他州、新墨西哥州和科罗拉多州。

sentences.en: Its annual flow is decreasing precipitously.
sentences.zh: 它的年径流量正在急剧减少。

sentences.en: But now, for years, states and the federal government have tried to cut the use of that water.
sentences.zh: 多年来，各州和联邦政府一直试图削减用水量。

sentences.en: But it hasn't worked.
sentences.zh: 但并没有奏效。

sentences.en: They haven't cut enough.
sentences.zh: 他们削减的还不够多。

sentences.en: And so, last year, as those levels got really low, officials said, we have to do more.
sentences.zh: 所以去年，随着水位降至极低，官员们表示，我们必须采取更多行动。

sentences.en: So, last summer, the federal government said, we want these seven states to find a deal to cut their total water use by 2 to 4 million acre feet.
sentences.zh: 因此，去年夏天，联邦政府表示，我们希望这七个州能达成协议，将总用水量削减 200 万到 400 万英亩英尺。

sentences.en: That's about 20 to 40 percent of the total flow of the river.
sentences.zh: 这大约是河流总流量的 20% 到 40%。

sentences.en: It's just an astonishing amount of water.
sentences.zh: 这简直是一个惊人的用水量。

sentences.en: 20 to 40 percent of the flow of the river.
sentences.zh: 河流流量的 20% 到 40%。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's almost inconceivable.
sentences.zh: 这几乎是不可想象的。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: But the government said, we've got no choice.
sentences.zh: 但政府表示，我们别无选择。

sentences.en: The situation is so dire.
sentences.zh: 情况太严峻了。

sentences.en: You, the states, have to make this cut.
sentences.zh: 你们这些州必须做出削减。

sentences.en: Please come to an agreement.
sentences.zh: 请达成一致。

sentences.en: They gave them a deadline of two months.
sentences.zh: 他们给了两个月的最后期限。

sentences.en: The states blew that deadline.
sentences.zh: 各州错过了那个期限。

sentences.en: There was no deal.
sentences.zh: 没有达成任何协议。

sentences.en: So, last fall, the government again said, really, states, we need you to come to a deal to make significant cuts.
sentences.zh: 所以去年秋天，政府再次表示，各州，我们真的需要你们达成协议，进行大幅削减。

sentences.en: And the deadline for that second round was today, Tuesday.
sentences.zh: 而第二轮谈判的截止日期就是今天，星期二。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: And I spent the last few weeks talking to negotiators from the states, and they all tell me the same thing.
sentences.zh: 过去几周我一直在与各州的谈判代表交谈，他们都告诉我同样的事情。

sentences.en: And it is extremely unlikely that they're going to reach a deal to make the magnitude of cuts the government wants.
sentences.zh: 他们极不可能达成政府所要求的削减幅度的协议。

sentences.en: And what exactly would happen if they don't reduce their water usage, Chris?
sentences.zh: 克里斯，如果他们不减少用水量，到底会发生什么？

sentences.en: I mean, what's the actual problem that they're trying to solve?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们试图解决的实际问题是什么？

sentences.en: In a word, it's Deadpool.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，就是“死池”状态。

sentences.en: And Deadpool is coming up faSt.
sentences.zh: 而且“死池”正迅速逼近。

sentences.en: Deadpool.
sentences.zh: 死池。

sentences.en: Okay, what's Deadpool?
sentences.zh: 好吧，什么是死池？

sentences.en: Large man-made reservoirs like Lake Mead could become a Deadpool.
sentences.zh: 像米德湖这样的大型人工水库可能会变成死池。

sentences.en: Deadpool.
sentences.zh: 死池。

sentences.en: Deadpool.
sentences.zh: 死池。

sentences.en: Deadpool is when Mead gets low enough to crash the whole Colorado system.
sentences.zh: 死池是指米德湖的水位降得太低，导致整个科罗拉多河系统瘫痪。

sentences.en: I am genuinely worried about the possibility of this system hitting Deadpool.
sentences.zh: 我真心担心这个系统会陷入死池状态。

sentences.en: You are.
sentences.zh: 你是认真的吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely, I am.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: So, let's take a step back.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们退一步来看。

sentences.en: And remember, at the center of this Colorado River system is two man-made lakes, Lake Powell and Lake Mead, both created by erecting enormous daMs.
sentences.zh: 记住，科罗拉多河系统的核心是两个人工湖，鲍威尔湖和米德湖，它们都是通过建造巨大的水坝形成的。

sentences.en: The lakes are for drinking water, reservoirs.
sentences.zh: 这些湖泊是饮用水源，是水库。

sentences.en: They also provide hydropower and flood control.
sentences.zh: 它们还提供水力发电和防洪功能。

sentences.en: They're crucial to the system.
sentences.zh: 它们对整个系统至关重要。

sentences.en: And there's two sorts of red lines that we're approaching as the drought gets worse.
sentences.zh: 随着干旱加剧，我们正在接近两条红线。

sentences.en: The first red line is if the water level in these two lakes gets low enough, these dams can't produce power anymore.
sentences.zh: 第一条红线是，如果这两个湖泊的水位降得足够低，这些水坝就无法再发电了。

sentences.en: That's a pretty significant hit for this region.
sentences.zh: 这对该地区来说是一个相当大的打击。

sentences.en: It's not the end of the world.
sentences.zh: 虽然不是世界末日。

sentences.en: These aren't the only sources of power, but it's a big problem.
sentences.zh: 这些并不是唯一的电力来源，但这是一个大问题。

sentences.en: The next red line is way worse.
sentences.zh: 下一条红线要糟糕得多。

sentences.en: The next red line you get to is Deadpool.
sentences.zh: 你到达的下一条红线就是死池。

sentences.en: At Deadpool, there's not enough water in these lakes for any water to pass through the daMs.
sentences.zh: 在死池状态下，湖里的水不够，无法流过水坝。

sentences.en: And what that means is these downstream states, California, Arizona, Nevada,
sentences.zh: 这意味着下游的各州，加利福尼亚州、亚利桑那州、内华达州，

sentences.en: they're losing what are in some cases their main source of drinking water and their main source of irrigation water.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，他们正在失去主要的饮用水源和主要的灌溉水源。

sentences.en: So as bad as no power is, no water at all passing through these dams is almost catastrophic for the lower half of this basin.
sentences.zh: 所以，虽然没电很糟糕，但完全没有水流过这些水坝对流域下半部分来说几乎是灾难性的。

sentences.en: And that's the one point everyone agrees on, the federal government and the seven states.
sentences.zh: 这一点是联邦政府和七个州唯一达成共识的地方。

sentences.en: Everybody wants to avoid Deadpool.
sentences.zh: 每个人都想避免死池。

sentences.en: But the question is, how do they do it?
sentences.zh: 但问题是，他们该怎么做？

sentences.en: So how close are we to this nightmare scenario you're describing?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们距离你描述的这种噩梦场景还有多近？

sentences.en: Well, when you physically look at the lakes, you can tell right away how incredibly low they are.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当你亲眼看到这些湖泊时，你立刻就能看出它们的水位低得惊人。

sentences.en: Wow, this lake is so shallow right now.
sentences.zh: 哇，这个湖现在太浅了。

sentences.en: You can see the sides of the basins where there's the so-called bathtub ring areas that used to be wet and are now bone dry.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到盆地的侧面，那些所谓的“浴缸环”区域，曾经被水覆盖，现在却干涸得一滴水都没有。

sentences.en: We were able to see handfuls of previously sunken boats that used to be at the bottom of the lake, and now they're just sitting completely dry on the shore.
sentences.zh: 我们能看到一些以前沉没的船只，它们曾经在湖底，现在却完全干涸地搁在岸上。

sentences.en: You can see exposed parts of the lake bed.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到暴露出来的湖床部分。

sentences.en: As the lake level recedes, secrets emerge.
sentences.zh: 随着湖水水位下降，秘密也随之浮现。

sentences.en: You can see in some places things that used to be buried, like old boats, even in some cases.
sentences.zh: 在某些地方，你可以看到曾经被掩埋的东西，比如旧船，甚至在某些情况下，

sentences.en: Like a body found in what's left of a metal barrel.
sentences.zh: 比如在一个金属桶里发现的一具尸体。

sentences.en: Bodies that have turned up.
sentences.zh: 陆续出现的尸体。

sentences.en: Four bodies have been discovered as the lake dries up.
sentences.zh: 随着湖水干涸，已经发现了四具尸体。

sentences.en: But the scary thing here is that no one really knows with much certainty when Deadpool could arrive.
sentences.zh: 但这里最可怕的是，没有人能确定死池何时会到来。

sentences.en: And the reason no one really knows is for a long time there was a fairly predictable relationship between how much snow fell in the mountains and how much of that water reached the river through snow melts.
sentences.zh: 之所以没人确定，是因为长期以来，山区降雪量与通过融雪流入河流的水量之间存在着相当可预测的关系。

sentences.en: What's happened recently is that relationship has broken down.
sentences.zh: 最近发生的情况是，这种关系已经破裂了。

sentences.en: So, what I heard from sources is that last year, there was almost average snowpack, but well below average stream flows.
sentences.zh: 我从消息来源听到的是，去年积雪量接近平均水平，但河流流量却远低于平均水平。

sentences.en: Year before that, also, almost average snowpack, but only about a third of average flows.
sentences.zh: 前一年也是如此，积雪量接近平均水平，但流量只有平均水平的三分之一左右。

sentences.en: So, if you lose that relationship, that connection between how much snow falls and how much water flows to the streams into the river,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你失去了这种联系，即降雪量与流入河流的径流量之间的联系，

sentences.en: it becomes really hard to predict how fast the system dries up.
sentences.zh: 就很难预测系统干涸的速度。

sentences.en: So, that's probably the worst place to be, where you lose your ability to predict just how fast these systems could disappear.
sentences.zh: 所以，这可能是最糟糕的情况，你失去了预测这些系统消失速度的能力。

sentences.en: So, you're saying that it could happen anytime, basically.
sentences.zh: 所以你是说，基本上随时都可能发生。

sentences.en: Like, we don't really know what the timing of this is.
sentences.zh: 我们真的不知道具体的时间点。

sentences.en: And look, it doesn't seem like anyone thinks this could happen tomorrow and probably won't happen this year.
sentences.zh: 听着，似乎没人认为这明天就会发生，今年大概也不会发生。

sentences.en: But definitely a concern for the year after and the year after that.
sentences.zh: 但这绝对是明年以及后年需要担心的问题。

sentences.en: But really, the point to underline is all the models that used to inform how much water would be in these lakes are breaking down because of climate change,
sentences.zh: 但真正需要强调的是，所有曾经用于预测湖泊水量的模型都因为气候变化而失效了，

sentences.en: because the pattern of precipitation is changing, the temperature in the air is changing.
sentences.zh: 因为降水模式正在改变，空气温度也在改变。

sentences.en: So, we no longer have as solid a grasp about how much time we have.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们不再能准确掌握我们还有多少时间。

sentences.en: So, the government has to not just work on really tight timelines, but also acknowledge we can't be sure of anything anymore.
sentences.zh: 因此，政府不仅必须在非常紧迫的时间表下工作，还必须承认我们对任何事情都无法再确定了。

sentences.en: And so, everyone's trying to move as fast as they can in case we have even less time than we think.
sentences.zh: 所以，每个人都在尽可能快地行动，以防我们的时间比想象中还要少。

sentences.en: So, the states are told they have to come to some agreement, right, on reducing their water usage.
sentences.zh: 所以，各州被告知必须就减少用水量达成某种协议，对吧？

sentences.en: But they can't seem to do it.
sentences.zh: 但他们似乎做不到。

sentences.en: Why can't they come to an agreement?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们无法达成协议？

sentences.en: The answer to that question starts 100 years ago.
sentences.zh: 这个问题的答案要追溯到 100 年前。

sentences.en: Back in 1922, the states argued over and finally agreed on how to apportion the water from the Colorado River.
sentences.zh: 早在 1922 年，各州就如何分配科罗拉多河的水量进行了争论，并最终达成了一致。

sentences.en: They knew even then that Colorado is the key to their survival in terms of human habitation, irrigation, building cities.
sentences.zh: 即使在当时，他们也知道科罗拉多河是他们人类居住、灌溉和城市建设生存的关键。

sentences.en: And that deal from 1922, called the Colorado River Compact, has really held together over the last century.
sentences.zh: 而那份 1922 年的协议，即《科罗拉多河契约》，在过去一个世纪里确实维持了下来。

sentences.en: And it remains the foundation of how they interact.
sentences.zh: 它仍然是他们互动的基础。

sentences.en: But the problem is, that deal was really based on a fiction.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，那份协议实际上是建立在虚构的基础上的。

sentences.en: Even at the time, the amount of water that was assumed to be running through the river every year was rarely as high as it thought it was going to be.
sentences.zh: 即使在当时，假设每年流经河流的水量也极少达到预期的水平。

sentences.en: And because of population growth and now climate change, there's more and more pressure.
sentences.zh: 而且由于人口增长和现在的气候变化，压力越来越大。

sentences.en: So, the actual water flow through that river keeps getting farther and farther below the number that holds up this whole deal.
sentences.zh: 因此，流经那条河流的实际水量不断低于支撑整个协议的数字。

sentences.en: So, Chris, they just miscalculated from the beginning?
sentences.zh: 所以，克里斯，他们从一开始就计算错误了吗？

sentences.en: You know, you could say they miscalculated.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你可以说他们计算错误了。

sentences.en: You could say it was wishful thinking.
sentences.zh: 你也可以说那是自欺欺人。

sentences.en: But whatever the cause, the number that underlay this whole deal, 17.5 million acre feet of water every year, was just wrong.
sentences.zh: 但无论原因是什么，支撑整个协议的数字，即每年 1750 万英亩英尺的水量，就是错误的。

sentences.en: Oh, man.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Most years over the last century, it's been below that.
sentences.zh: 过去一个世纪里，大多数年份的流量都低于这个数字。

sentences.en: And the last 20 years, it's been dangerously below that.
sentences.zh: 而在过去的 20 年里，它一直处于危险的低位。

sentences.en: And that number keeps on shrinking almost every year.
sentences.zh: 而且这个数字几乎每年都在不断缩小。

sentences.en: So, really, what's happening here is a deal that was never really quite based on fact is colliding with the reality of climate change.
sentences.zh: 所以，实际上这里发生的是，一份从未真正基于事实的协议正在与气候变化的现实发生碰撞。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: So, basically, all this development in the West, you know, the growth of agriculture in Southern California, the growth of cities like Phoenix,
sentences.zh: 所以，基本上，西部所有的这些发展，你知道，南加州农业的增长，凤凰城等城市的扩张，

sentences.en: was all based on a flawed assumption.
sentences.zh: 都是基于一个错误的假设。

sentences.en: That there would be way more water than there ever actually was.
sentences.zh: 即水资源会比实际情况多得多。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the consequences of that flawed assumption just grew over time.
sentences.zh: 而那个错误假设的后果随着时间的推移而不断扩大。

sentences.en: Because based on those assumptions, cities emerged and got bigger.
sentences.zh: 因为基于这些假设，城市出现了并变得更大。

sentences.en: Communities got bigger.
sentences.zh: 社区变得更大。

sentences.en: Farmers planted more crops.
sentences.zh: 农民种植了更多的农作物。

sentences.en: So, the demand on that river grew.
sentences.zh: 因此，对那条河流的需求增加了。

sentences.en: And at the same time, especially in the last 20 years, the supply of water has shrunk even more dramatically because of the drought and the effects of climate change.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，特别是在过去 20 年里，由于干旱和气候变化的影响，供水量缩减得更加剧烈。

sentences.en: So, this deal, this sort of foundational agreement is under pressure from both sides.
sentences.zh: 所以，这份协议，这种基础性的契约，正受到来自两方面的压力。

sentences.en: More demand and less water.
sentences.zh: 需求增加，水量减少。

sentences.en: And last year and this year are really the point where it becomes obvious to everyone.
sentences.zh: 去年和今年确实是每个人都显而易见意识到这一点的时刻。

sentences.en: It's just untenable.
sentences.zh: 这简直是难以为继的。

sentences.en: So, what exactly are these states arguing?
sentences.zh: 那么，这些州到底在争论什么？

sentences.en: I mean, what does the fight look like?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这场争斗是什么样的？

sentences.en: Well, there's two basic groups.
sentences.zh: 嗯，主要有两个基本阵营。

sentences.en: Upper Basin and Lower Basin.
sentences.zh: 上游流域和下游流域。

sentences.en: Let's start with the Upper Basin.
sentences.zh: 让我们从上游流域开始。

sentences.en: The Upper Basin are four states.
sentences.zh: 上游流域包括四个州。

sentences.en: Colorado, New Mexico, Utah, and Wyoming.
sentences.zh: 科罗拉多州、新墨西哥州、犹他州和怀俄明州。

sentences.en: They're kind of a group.
sentences.zh: 他们算是一个阵营。

sentences.en: What makes them a group is that they are all upstream of these two reservoirs, Lake Powell and Lake Mead.
sentences.zh: 它们之所以被称为一个群体，是因为它们都位于鲍威尔湖和米德湖这两个水库的上游。

sentences.en: So, the important thing with the upstream states is they don't rely on giant reservoirs to just pull their water from.
sentences.zh: 所以，上游各州的关键在于，它们并不单纯依赖大型水库来获取水源。

sentences.en: They are sort of dependent on whatever the stream flow is.
sentences.zh: 它们在某种程度上取决于河流的流量。

sentences.en: And as the snow melts in the Rocky Mountains has gone down, the amount of water reaching these states has dropped precipitously.
sentences.zh: 随着落基山脉的积雪融化量减少，流向这些州的水量也急剧下降。

sentences.en: I'm told they're getting about half as much as their actual allotment.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，它们目前获得的水量大约只有实际分配额的一半。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: Is the amount of actual water reaching the mostly farmers' fields in these states.
sentences.zh: 这是流向这些州农田的实际水量。

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太惊人了。

sentences.en: So, their argument is don't look to us.
sentences.zh: 所以，它们的论点是：别指望我们。

sentences.en: We're already at half of our paper rights for water.
sentences.zh: 我们纸面上的用水权已经减半了。

sentences.en: So, how can you ask us to go much lower?
sentences.zh: 所以，你怎么能要求我们再进一步削减呢？

sentences.en: We can't be the solution.
sentences.zh: 我们不可能是解决办法。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We're already down by half.
sentences.zh: 我们已经减了一半了。

sentences.en: So, no way.
sentences.zh: 所以，没门。

sentences.en: Not us.
sentences.zh: 别找我们。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And so, that just leaves the three lower-based states, which are Nevada, Arizona, and California.
sentences.zh: 这样一来，就只剩下下游的三个州了，即内华达州、亚利桑那州和加利福尼亚州。

sentences.en: And Nevada is pretty straightforward.
sentences.zh: 内华达州的情况比较简单明了。

sentences.en: They already get almost no water.
sentences.zh: 它们本来就几乎没有水。

sentences.en: They have an allotment of 300,000 acre-feet.
sentences.zh: 它们的分配额是30万英亩英尺。

sentences.en: It's a sliver in the pie.
sentences.zh: 这只是蛋糕的一小块。

sentences.en: Even if you just cut off Nevada entirely, it wouldn't get the government that much closer to its goal.
sentences.zh: 即使你完全切断内华达州的供水，政府也无法离目标更近多少。

sentences.en: And Nevada says, well, hang on.
sentences.zh: 而内华达州则说，等等。

sentences.en: We're already doing a lot anyway to reduce our water use.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，我们已经在减少用水量方面做了很多工作。

sentences.en: The state even passed a law last year outlawing some kinds of grass lawns.
sentences.zh: 该州去年甚至通过了一项法律，禁止了某些类型的草坪。

sentences.en: So, their argument is don't look to us.
sentences.zh: 所以，它们的论点是：别指望我们。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, that leaves just two states.
sentences.zh: 所以，只剩下两个州了。

sentences.en: Arizona and California.
sentences.zh: 亚利桑那州和加利福尼亚州。

sentences.en: Which happen to be the two states that actually use the most water.
sentences.zh: 巧合的是，这两个州恰恰是用水量最大的州。

sentences.en: And they've got something else in common, which is both states say more cuts should come from the other state.
sentences.zh: 它们还有另一个共同点，那就是两个州都认为应该削减对方的用水量。

sentences.en: But what makes those two states really interesting is they have just fundamentally different arguments and different philosophies about how this should be decided.
sentences.zh: 但这两个州真正有趣的地方在于，它们在如何决策的问题上，有着根本不同的论点和哲学理念。

sentences.en: So, what looks at first glance like a battle between states is really a battle between two competing ideas.
sentences.zh: 所以，乍看之下是州与州之间的博弈，实则是两种竞争理念之间的较量。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 430 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点30分给总统打了电话，他接听了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空探索七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today, I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天，我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 它们可能每年都是联盟中最强的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的首字母单词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅出的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: Celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 庆祝175年来帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，享受nytimes.com/subscribe的特别优惠。

sentences.en: Okay, Chris.
sentences.zh: 好的，克里斯。

sentences.en: So, this big question about how to reduce the water use of the Colorado River is, as you just laid out for us,
sentences.zh: 那么，关于如何减少科罗拉多河用水量的这个大问题，正如你刚才为我们梳理的那样，

sentences.en: basically coming down to a dispute between California on the one side and Arizona on the other.
sentences.zh: 归根结底是加利福尼亚州和亚利桑那州之间的争端。

sentences.en: And you said they had two really different approaches.
sentences.zh: 你说它们有两种截然不同的处理方式。

sentences.en: So, what are these approaches?
sentences.zh: 那么，这些方式是什么呢？

sentences.en: Tell me about them.
sentences.zh: 跟我说说吧。

sentences.en: So, let's start with California.
sentences.zh: 那么，我们先从加利福尼亚州说起。

sentences.en: California, and we should say it's the southern part of the state that's getting this water.
sentences.zh: 加利福尼亚州，我们应该说明的是，获得这些水的是该州的南部地区。

sentences.en: It's Los Angeles and San Diego.
sentences.zh: 也就是洛杉矶和圣地亚哥。

sentences.en: And most of all, it's farmers in the Imperial Valley and other parts of the southern part of the state.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，帝国谷和该州南部其他地区的农民。

sentences.en: This sort of breadbasket of America.
sentences.zh: 这里堪称美国的粮仓。

sentences.en: And southern California is making what boils down to a legal argument.
sentences.zh: 而南加州提出的论点归根结底是一个法律论点。

sentences.en: The way the laws of the river work is that different users have different priorities based on how long they've been used in the water.
sentences.zh: 河流法律的运作方式是，不同的用户根据使用水资源的时间长短拥有不同的优先权。

sentences.en: And California, southern California, has really the most senior rights in the system.
sentences.zh: 而加利福尼亚州，即南加州，确实拥有该系统中资历最老的用水权。

sentences.en: So, before California gets cut, others, in particular Arizona, are supposed to get cut firSt.
sentences.zh: 因此，在加利福尼亚州被削减之前，其他人，特别是亚利桑那州，应该先被削减。

sentences.en: So, California says, look, our legal basis is strong.
sentences.zh: 所以，加利福尼亚州说，看，我们的法律依据很充分。

sentences.en: We don't have to take these cuts.
sentences.zh: 我们不必接受这些削减。

sentences.en: They should go to somebody else firSt.
sentences.zh: 它们应该先由别人承担。

sentences.en: And only once Arizona goes dry do you come to us.
sentences.zh: 只有当亚利桑那州干涸了，才会轮到我们。

sentences.en: Now, it's not their only argument.
sentences.zh: 当然，这并不是它们唯一的论点。

sentences.en: California also says that because they produce so much of the vegetables and even hay for cows,
sentences.zh: 加利福尼亚州还表示，因为它们生产了全国大量的蔬菜，甚至还有奶牛吃的干草，

sentences.en: around the country, if California were to be meaningfully cut, you would have a food crisis.
sentences.zh: 如果加利福尼亚州的用水量被大幅削减，就会引发粮食危机。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But their main argument is on the law.
sentences.zh: 但它们的主要论点还是基于法律。

sentences.en: And everyone I talked to for this story said that on the law itself, California is mostly right.
sentences.zh: 我为这个报道采访过的每个人都说，就法律本身而言，加利福尼亚州大体上是正确的。

sentences.en: That's not the dispute.
sentences.zh: 争议点不在这里。

sentences.en: The dispute is how much will that argument count for against Arizona's case.
sentences.zh: 争议在于，相对于亚利桑那州的诉求，这一论点会有多大的分量。

sentences.en: So, what's Arizona's case?
sentences.zh: 那么，亚利桑那州的诉求是什么呢？

sentences.en: Arizona makes a very different argument.
sentences.zh: 亚利桑那州提出了一个非常不同的论点。

sentences.en: And the negotiators I spoke with conceded that their legal argument isn't that strong.
sentences.zh: 我交谈过的谈判代表承认，它们的法律论点并不那么强有力。

sentences.en: But they say they've got different arguments.
sentences.zh: 但它们说它们有其他的论点。

sentences.en: The main one is what's practical and what's fair.
sentences.zh: 主要的一点是关于实际情况和公平性。

sentences.en: They say that most of the farmers in Arizona who rely on this water have already suffered and lost a lot of that water.
sentences.zh: 它们说，亚利桑那州大多数依赖这些水资源的农民已经遭受了损失，失去了大量的水。

sentences.en: It really comes down to cities, Phoenix and Tucson, and also tribes.
sentences.zh: 这实际上归结为城市问题，即凤凰城和图森市，以及原住民部落的问题。

sentences.en: A significant number of Native American tribes are along these canals in Arizona, and they would be hurt too.
sentences.zh: 亚利桑那州的这些运河沿岸有相当多的美洲原住民部落，他们也会受到伤害。

sentences.en: So, Arizona says, sure, on the law, maybe you can cut us firSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，亚利桑那州说，当然，从法律上讲，也许你们可以先削减我们的用水量。

sentences.en: But in reality, it makes no sense.
sentences.zh: 但在现实中，这毫无意义。

sentences.en: You would be causing significant health harms to these cities, and the government would be violating its obligations to tribes that have been promised this water through treaties.
sentences.zh: 你们会给这些城市造成严重的健康危害，政府也会违背通过条约向部落承诺提供这些水的义务。

sentences.en: So, Arizona's argument boils down to, don't just look at the law, look at what makes sense.
sentences.zh: 所以，亚利桑那州的论点归结为：不要只看法律，要看什么才是合理的。

sentences.en: And if you look at what makes sense, you cannot cut us that deep because people would suffer too much.
sentences.zh: 如果你看什么才是合理的，你就不能削减我们这么多，因为人们会遭受太大的痛苦。

sentences.en: I mean, Arizona is basically saying to California, we're talking about people and drinking water and being able to bathe.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，亚利桑那州基本上是在对加利福尼亚州说，我们谈论的是人、饮用水和洗澡的问题。

sentences.en: I mean, this is more important than some cabbages or some almond farMs.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这比一些卷心菜或杏仁农场重要得多。

sentences.en: Yeah, and it's a really compelling argument.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个非常有说服力的论点。

sentences.en: But at the same time, California has what seems like a compelling argument, which is,
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，加利福尼亚州也有一个看起来很有说服力的论点，那就是：

sentences.en: was it a good idea in the first place for Arizona to build these cities in the desert that rely on a supply of water whose legal foundation was never that solid, right?
sentences.zh: 当初亚利桑那州在沙漠中建立这些依赖于法律基础从未稳固的水源的城市，这真的是个好主意吗？

sentences.en: And I think the intractability of these negotiations really comes down to the fact that both sides have good arguments, but they're good in different ways.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些谈判的棘手之处在于，双方都有很好的论点，但它们在不同层面上都是合理的。

sentences.en: And nobody is quite willing to agree to a deal that imposes really severe harm on their own constituents.
sentences.zh: 而且没有人愿意同意一项会给自己的选民带来严重伤害的协议。

sentences.en: And I don't know how you get around that dynamic.
sentences.zh: 我不知道该如何打破这种僵局。

sentences.en: So what are they going to do?
sentences.zh: 那么它们打算怎么做？

sentences.en: What happens now?
sentences.zh: 现在会发生什么？

sentences.en: So the federal government, having failed last summer to get states to make a deal, try it again.
sentences.zh: 所以联邦政府在去年夏天未能促成各州达成协议后，又尝试了一次。

sentences.en: And in November, they said to the states, all right, here's what's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 在11月，它们对各州说，好吧，接下来会发生这样的事。

sentences.en: We're going to start a process to study the effects of significantly cutting water use from the Colorado.
sentences.zh: 我们将启动一个程序，研究大幅削减科罗拉多河用水量的影响。

sentences.en: And we want you to give us a plan that we can study.
sentences.zh: 我们希望你们给我们一个我们可以研究的计划。

sentences.en: Because if we don't have a plan from you, we'll just make a plan of our own.
sentences.zh: 因为如果我们没有你们的计划，我们就会自己制定一个。

sentences.en: And that'll be what happens.
sentences.zh: 事情就会变成那样。

sentences.en: Because there's a ticking clock here.
sentences.zh: 因为这里有一个紧迫的时间表。

sentences.en: The government has to have a plan in place that's been studied by the summer, which is when evaporation is highest, temperatures are higheSt.
sentences.zh: 政府必须在夏季之前制定出一份经过研究的计划，因为那时蒸发量最高，气温也最高。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The threat of Deadpool is looming.
sentences.zh: “死池”的威胁正在逼近。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The threat of Deadpool is highest because these lakes will shrink even more.
sentences.zh: “死池”的威胁最大，因为这些湖泊会进一步萎缩。

sentences.en: So this isn't some arbitrary timeline.
sentences.zh: 所以这不是一个随意的截止日期。

sentences.en: The government has said to states, if you want to be involved in this and have us study your plan, give it to us by the end of January.
sentences.zh: 政府已经对各州说，如果你们想参与其中并让我们研究你们的计划，请在1月底前交给我们。

sentences.en: And that's the deadline that states now seem unable to meet.
sentences.zh: 而这似乎是各州目前无法满足的最后期限。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So now the federal government has to find a plan of its own because it won't have a plan from the states.
sentences.zh: 所以现在联邦政府必须找到自己的计划，因为它不会有来自各州的计划。

sentences.en: And the federal government is concerned that if there isn't a plan the states have agreed on,
sentences.zh: 联邦政府担心，如果没有各州同意的计划，

sentences.en: that sets up a very real risk that whatever the government does gets mired in legal fights,
sentences.zh: 这会带来一个非常现实的风险，即政府所做的任何事情都会陷入法律纠纷，

sentences.en: which could slow down the whole process and make it harder to act with the urgency that's required.
sentences.zh: 这可能会拖慢整个进程，使我们更难采取所需的紧急行动。

sentences.en: Like a delay that they can't really afford.
sentences.zh: 就像它们无法承受的延误一样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So we don't know yet how these cuts will actually be distributed, but it's a pretty safe bet that it's going to be some combination of the following.
sentences.zh: 所以我们还不知道这些削减将如何实际分配，但可以肯定的是，它将是以下各项的某种组合。

sentences.en: Probably some portion of farmers in California won't have water to irrigate their crops.
sentences.zh: 加利福尼亚州的部分农民可能将没有水来灌溉农作物。

sentences.en: They'll have to fallow their fields.
sentences.zh: 他们将不得不让土地休耕。

sentences.en: Number two, cities in Arizona and quite possibly in Southern California will have to be even more aggressive and innovative and rushed about using less water,
sentences.zh: 第二，亚利桑那州甚至很可能是南加州的城市，将不得不更积极、更具创新性且更仓促地减少用水，

sentences.en: becoming more efficient and ripping up more lawns.
sentences.zh: 提高效率并拆除更多的草坪。

sentences.en: Tribes in Arizona in particular will see their access to water go down.
sentences.zh: 特别是亚利桑那州的部落，将看到它们的用水量减少。

sentences.en: These are communities that will suffer a lot if they lose access to water.
sentences.zh: 如果这些社区失去用水渠道，它们将遭受巨大的痛苦。

sentences.en: So this pain is going to be spread around, but the question that I think everyone is asking is, will the pain be so great in any one area that it's just unbearable?
sentences.zh: 所以这种痛苦将会蔓延，但我认为每个人都在问的问题是：任何一个地区的痛苦是否会大到无法承受？

sentences.en: And in some cases, these states are going to decide that they can't bear it and they need to find new sources of water, whether it's recycling, desalination,
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，这些州将决定它们无法承受，需要寻找新的水源，无论是循环利用、海水淡化，

sentences.en: maybe even bringing water in from somewhere else through pipelines.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能通过管道从其他地方引水。

sentences.en: So this isn't the end of the story.
sentences.zh: 所以这并不是故事的终点。

sentences.en: This is going to prompt a whole new wave of aggressive, risky, maybe not quite feasible strategies to try and get more water.
sentences.zh: 这将引发新一轮积极、冒险、甚至可能不太可行的策略，试图获取更多的水。

sentences.en: So really, we're back to where we were 100 years ago.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，我们又回到了100年前的原点。

sentences.en: They've got to figure out where to get more water.
sentences.zh: 它们必须想办法从哪里获得更多的水。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Back then, the West looked around and, you know, saw a landscape that was mostly desert, but decided not to accept that reality.
sentences.zh: 那时，西部地区环顾四周，看到了大部分是沙漠的景观，但决定不接受这一现实。

sentences.en: And instead decided to do these really dramatic things to change that reality.
sentences.zh: 相反，它们决定采取这些非常戏剧性的举措来改变这一现实。

sentences.en: And you're saying they might do that again.
sentences.zh: 你是说它们可能会再次这样做。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Anyone who's been to this part of the country knows there is an almost magnetic draw, like an almost unearthly beauty that this part of the country has.
sentences.zh: 任何去过这个地区的人都知道，这里有一种几乎像磁铁般的吸引力，这个地区有一种近乎超凡脱俗的美。

sentences.en: And people can't get enough of it.
sentences.zh: 人们对它趋之若鹜。

sentences.en: And just like 100 years ago, they'll do whatever they can to make it livable and to grow there, even as the cost of that growth gets harder and harder to bear.
sentences.zh: 就像100年前一样，它们会尽其所能让这里变得宜居并在此发展，即使这种增长的代价变得越来越难以承受。

sentences.en: And the only question is, what will they try next?
sentences.zh: 唯一的问题是，它们接下来会尝试什么？

sentences.en: Chris, thank you.
sentences.zh: 克里斯，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wena Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是维娜·刘。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times Games.
sentences.zh: 我编写了《纽约时报》游戏中的谜题之一——《Connections》。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 而且我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 而且我喜欢尝试捉弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖尔斯基，我每天负责制作《拼字蜜蜂》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我还有一种叫联觉的特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚才听到的那些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 前往 nytimes.com/games 即可开始游玩。

sentences.en: Here's what else you should know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还应该了解的消息。

sentences.en: On Monday, the fallout from the death of Tyree Nichols, the 29-year-old who was violently beaten by police in Memphis, continued.
sentences.zh: 周一，29岁的泰瑞·尼科尔斯在孟菲斯遭警察暴力殴打致死事件的后续影响仍在持续。

sentences.en: After firing five officers, the city confirmed that it had removed two more officers from duty for their role in the encounter, one of whom fired a stun gun at Nichols.
sentences.zh: 在解雇了五名警官后，该市确认又将两名参与此事的警官停职，其中一人曾向尼科尔斯发射过电击枪。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the city's fire department fired two medics and a lieutenant for failing to follow protocols.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，该市消防部门解雇了两名医护人员和一名中尉，原因是他们未能遵守规程。

sentences.en: Video footage of the incident show the medics failing to treat Nichols after he was beaten.
sentences.zh: 事件的视频录像显示，这两名医护人员在尼科尔斯被殴打后未能对其进行救治。

sentences.en: And in Pakistan, a powerful bombing ripped through a mosque in Peshawar, a northern provincial capital near the border with Afghanistan,
sentences.zh: 在巴基斯坦，白沙瓦的一座清真寺发生了一起强力爆炸，白沙瓦是靠近阿富汗边境的一个北部省会城市，

sentences.en: killing at least 60 people and injuring at least 157.
sentences.zh: 造成至少60人死亡，157人受伤。

sentences.en: The suicide bombing was the worst attack in the country in months, and comes as violence near the border has been rising, especially against Pakistan's police and military.
sentences.zh: 这起自杀式爆炸袭击是该国数月来最严重的袭击事件，发生之际，边境附近的暴力活动正日益加剧，尤其是针对巴基斯坦警察和军队的袭击。

sentences.en: The mosque that was hit on Monday was frequented by police officers.
sentences.zh: 周一遇袭的这座清真寺常有警官出入。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Michael Simon Johnson and Will Reed, with help from Claire Tennesketter.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由迈克尔·西蒙·约翰逊和威尔·里德制作，克莱尔·特内斯凯特提供了协助。

sentences.en: It was edited by Paige Cowett, contains original music by Marian Lozano and Dan Powell, and was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 节目由佩奇·考维特剪辑，包含玛丽安·洛萨诺和丹·鲍威尔的原创音乐，并由克里斯·伍德负责工程制作。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Bunberg and Ben Lansford of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly的吉姆·邦伯格和本·兰斯福德创作。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》节目中，我们将为假期接待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 敬请收听，获取让客人宾至如归的小贴士。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要全黑环境才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会喝到断片才去睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线条件？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为那是非常具体的要求。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢的任何播客平台上收听《Wirecutter秀》。
